overview: 84 official Qs (2008, 2017, 2019, 2025). Agriculture dominates (production 11, PDS 12, finance 9, productivity 7), industry patterns 13; services, NIP 1991, EoDB and IT are small; procurement and disinvestment not yet asked. Mostly one-liners (45 + 26 without printed options), 8 negative, few statement/matching. Facts asked: scheme–agency pairs, policy–year pairs, steel-plant collaborators, AP PDS numbers, dated shares.

possibility.angle: Cropping pattern, holdings and farm organisation
possibility.what_they_ask: holding size classes (marginal < 1 ha), cash vs food crop, largest cropping system (rice–wheat), features of joint co-operative farming

possibility.angle: Agricultural production – Green Revolution, phases, crop ranks, NAP 2000
possibility.what_they_ask: crop that gained most (wheat), names linked to Green Revolution, foodgrains definition, top Bt-cotton state, India's milk/fruit rank, NAP 4% target, horticulture overtaking foodgrains
BGREI crop (paddy), highest fertiliser subsidy (urea), launch plan/year of RKVY, NMSA, PMKSY, AP Indira Prabha

possibility.angle: Agricultural finance – NABARD, RRBs, crop insurance, SHG linkage
possibility.what_they_ask: what NABARD does directly and what it does not supervise, who prepares PLPs, RRB committee, crop-insurance exclusions, RWBCIS aim, livestock credit-guarantee agency

possibility.angle: Agricultural marketing – Agmark, e-NAM, contract farming, BIS
possibility.what_they_ask: Central Agmark lab (Nagpur), who issues AGMARK, e-auction meaning, contract farming terms
who determines MSP (CACP recommends, CCEA decides), Swaminathan Commission year, MSP figure for a season, central issue price definition, old AP rice price

possibility.evidence: 0 Qs; related APPSC Qs touch FCI/food security
possibility.what_they_ask: natural targets: FCI (1965) role, decentralised procurement (1997-98), economic cost vs MSP vs CIP, buffer norms – judged from how MSP/CIP items are asked

possibility.angle: Distribution – PDS/TPDS/NFSA and AP ration system
possibility.what_they_ask: TPDS year (1997), NFSA coverage 75/50, AP fair-price-shop counts and density, white-card share and income limit, AP PDS reform features, food-security definition

possibility.angle: Industrial development – policies, steel plants, PSUs, SSI, SEZ, IIP/PMI
possibility.what_they_ask: IPR 1956/1977 focus, steel-plant collaborator country, first cotton mill, NMP 2011 targets, IIP periodicity, core-industry weights, SEZ primary aim

possibility.angle: Problems of industry and industrial sickness
possibility.what_they_ask: definition of a sick unit, Land Acquisition Act 1894 purpose, committee–subject matching, Factories Act 'occupier', venture capital; sickness causes/remedies not yet asked separately (natural targets: SICA 1985, BIFR, IBC 2016)

possibility.angle: New Industrial Policy 1991 and competition law
possibility.what_they_ask: year licence raj ended, MRTP replaced by Competition Act 2002, convertibility clause removed

possibility.evidence: 0 Qs in Group 2; asked in other APPSC exams (CPSE stake-sale method, effect on backward states)
possibility.what_they_ask: natural targets: Rangarajan Committee 1993, DIPAM (2016), NIF, strategic vs minority sale, New PSE Policy 2021
services share of GDP vs employment, 2017-18 share 54.4%, insurance penetration definition, gig-economy leader, largest tech employer

traps.trap: [Partner] Swaps the foreign collaborator of a steel plant
traps.spot: Options list UK, USSR, West Germany, USA
traps.fix: Bhilai and Bokaro USSR; Rourkela West Germany; Durgapur UK

traps.trap: [Agency] Gives a decision to the advisory body (or NABARD a direct role)
traps.fix: CACP only recommends MSP – CCEA decides; NABARD refinances, does not lend to farmers directly
traps.pyq: MSP determined by → 'none of the given answers' (CACP recommends) [mains-2017-paper3#27]; NABARD lends directly to → 'None of the above' [group2-2008-paper3#3]

traps.trap: [Scope] Extends a body's supervision one level too far
traps.spot: NABARD option that adds 'including primary co-operative societies'
traps.fix: NABARD inspects RRBs, StCBs, DCCBs; PACS are under the state Registrar
traps.pyq: 'inspect RRBs and co-operative banks including primary co-operative societies' is not true [mains-2017-paper3#61]

traps.trap: [GDP vs jobs] Services output share swapped with employment share
traps.spot: Two questions on services with 'GDP' vs 'employment'
traps.fix: Services > 50% of GDP but about a fourth of employment (2000s)
traps.pyq: Services in GDP → 'more than 50%' [group2-2008-paper3#134]; in employment → 'a fourth' [group2-2008-paper3#135]

traps.trap: [Crop] Green Revolution crop or person swapped
traps.spot: Paddy vs wheat; a real politician among scientists
traps.fix: Biggest gain in wheat; names: Borlaug, Swaminathan, C. Subramaniam – not Swaran Singh
traps.pyq: Maximum increase → Wheat [prelims-2017#105]; not associated → Sardar Swaran Singh [prelims-2017#98]

traps.trap: [Policy year] Feature placed in the wrong industrial policy
traps.fix: 1956 public sector + licensing + small industry; 1977 small/village industry; 1991 delicensing
traps.pyq: IPR 1977 focussed on 'Small scale and village industry' [prelims-2017#111]; licence-permit raj abolished 1991 [prelims-2019#110]

traps.trap: [Anachronism] Later reform listed as an existing feature
traps.fix: ePoS, GPS vehicles, portability existed by 2017; doorstep delivery came in 2021
traps.pyq: Not a feature (2017) → 'Delivery of goods at doorstep' [mains-2017-paper3#135]

traps.fix: NFSA: 75% rural, 50% urban, about two-thirds overall

techniques.name: [Recommend vs decide] Who-advises / who-decides split
techniques.how: For MSP, credit plans, guarantees: name the recommending body and the deciding/implementing body; reject the one that only advises when the stem says 'determines'.
techniques.example: PLPs prepared by NABARD; district credit plan by lead bank → NABARD [mains-2019-paper2#87]

techniques.name: [Policy ladder] Industrial-policy ladder
techniques.how: 1948 mixed → 1956 three schedules, public sector, licensing → 1977 small/village → 1991 delicensing, MRTP pre-entry gone → 2002 Competition Act.
techniques.example: IPR 1956 provisions: licensing, public-sector expansion, small industries → all three (I, II, III) [mains-2025-paper2#9]

techniques.name: [Timeline] Food-security timeline
techniques.how: PDS → RPDS 1992 → TPDS 1997 → AAY 2000 → NFSA 2013; place each option on it.

techniques.name: [Exclusion] Natural vs man-made risk test
techniques.how: Crop-insurance covers non-preventable natural risks (drought, flood, pests); damage caused by the farmer's own action is excluded.
techniques.example: Not a condition → 'damage due to use of pesticides' [mains-2017-paper3#139]

techniques.name: [Match] Committee–subject matching by one fixed pair
techniques.how: Fix the surest pair first (Rangarajan–disinvestment), then eliminate codes that break it.
techniques.example: Tax administration–Shome, disinvestment–Rangarajan, SSI–Abid Hussain, sickness–Goswami → 1-D, 2-C, 3-B, 4-A [mains-2019-paper3#93]

techniques.name: [Magnitude] Order-of-magnitude check for AP figures
techniques.how: Compare option scale with population/households: a state of ~8 crore has crores of cards, tens of thousands of shops.
techniques.example: White ration cards in AP (2007) → 170 lakh, not 17 lakh [group2-2008-paper3#130]

confusions.remember: MSP paid to farmer; CIP charged to states for PDS
1956 public sector + licensing; 1977 small and village industries
First cotton mill vs first successful mill (Davar)
> 50% output, ~ a fourth to a third of jobs
Joint: voluntary, land rights kept; collective: ownership pooled
AGMARK by Directorate of Marketing & Inspection, not FAO
India leads supply (OLI); US leads demand

anchors: Holdings: < 1 ha marginal, 1–2 small, 2–4 semi-medium, 4–10 medium, ≥ 10 large
TPDS 1997; AAY 25 Dec 2000; NFSA 2013 – 75% rural, 50% urban
AP: about 30,000 fair-price shops (2017); one FPS per ~1,376 persons vs GoI norm 2,000
NABARD 1982; SHG–Bank linkage pilot by NABARD 1992; Narasimham 1975 → RRBs
IPR 1948, 1956, 1977; NIP 1991 ended licence raj; Competition Act 2002
NMP 2011: manufacturing 25% of GDP and 100 million jobs by 2022
IIP monthly; refinery products have the largest weight among core industries
India climbed 23 places in Doing Business (100 in 2018 report)
India 1st in milk; 2nd in fruits and vegetables
checklist: Scheme or body? Separate who recommends, who decides, who implements.
Industrial policy? Put the option on the 1948–1956–1977–1991 ladder.
AP PDS number? Check scale (lakh vs crore) and the year in the stem.
Share question? Confirm output (GDP/GVA) or employment, and the year.
'Not a feature' item? Date each feature; the later one is the misfit.
Crop/collaborator pair? Recall the fixed pair before reading options.
